steps.name: Sample structure QC (inherited context for the delivered DE table)
steps.question: Given the 6 AD-lesional vs 6 control skin samples in counts.csv/metadata.csv, does the sample structure (PCA on variance-stabilized counts, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) support the treated-vs-control contrast reported in de_results.csv, and how does the known low-depth sample (sample_01, ~4x below median library size) behave relative to its group?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC (vst blind, PCA on top-variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, explicit reporting of the flagged low-depth sample) per R-0033@40bf and R-0008@440d.

steps.description: Runs DESeq2 vst(blind=TRUE) on the raw counts, computes PCA on the top 500 most-variable genes, a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap, and per-sample library sizes/detected-gene counts, colored by condition (lesional vs control). Reports sample_01's position on PCA and its distance-heatmap block explicitly rather than silently dropping it, per the rule that a library size several-fold below the study median is a keep-inspect-report case, not an automatic exclusion. This step establishes whether the pre-computed de_results.csv contrast rests on an adequate sample structure; it does not re-fit DESeq2.
acceptance_criteria: PCA plot and sample-distance heatmap produced, colored by condition
Library size and detected-gene count reported per sample, sample_01 flagged and compared to the group median
A stated judgment on whether sample_01 should be flagged as an outlier for interpretation purposes, with reasoning, not a silent drop

steps.name: GO Biological Process over-representation (clusterProfiler enrichGO + rrvgo)
steps.question: Which GO Biological Process terms are over-represented among the genes significant (padj < 0.05) in the AD-lesional vs control contrast reported in de_results.csv, tested against the universe of all genes actually tested in that contrast?

grounding.reason: GO BP over-representation with clusterProfiler enrichGO (tested-genes universe, 15-500 size window, org.Hs.eg.db ID mapping) and rrvgo redundancy reduction per R-0095@492a; 50-gene ORA power caveat per R-0103@93aa; delivered-table direction/sign-convention statement per R-0110@41cb.

steps.description: Loads de_results.csv (gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, log2FC-related columns, padj, etc.) and defines the significant gene list as padj < 0.05 (the table's own adjusted p-value column; reports the exact cutoff and resulting list size). States explicitly: the universe is every gene present in de_results.csv (the tested genes, not the whole genome/annotation); gene symbols are mapped to Entrez IDs via org.Hs.eg.db (Bioconductor 3.23.1), with the unmapped/multiply-mapped share reported and those genes dropped with a stated count. Runs clusterProfiler::enrichGO (ont='BP') separately for (a) all significant genes pooled and (b) up-regulated and down-regulated genes as two separate lists (states the direction-handling choice and the log2FC sign convention/reference level exactly as used in de_results.csv), restricting GO term size to 15-500 genes among the tested set, with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. If the significant gene list has fewer than ~50 genes, the step does not force an ORA conclusion: it states the list size, still runs the test for completeness, but flags the result as underpowered/exploratory only, per the sourced rule. Significant GO BP terms (q < 0.05) are then reduced to non-redundant representative terms via rrvgo semantic similarity (rrvgo package), keeping the full un-reduced term table as a supplementary output. All gene IDs, universe definition, size window, adjustment method, and package/collection versions (clusterProfiler 4.20.0, org.Hs.eg.db 3.23.1, GO.db 3.23.1, rrvgo 1.24.0) are recorded for reproducibility.
acceptance_criteria: Significant gene list defined at padj<0.05 from de_results.csv, with the exact list size stated (and an explicit underpowered-ORA flag if <50 genes)

Unmapped/ambiguous gene-symbol-to-Entrez share reported

All collection/package versions and the padj cutoff recorded in the output

steps.name: Integrated report: GO BP enrichment results with QC context and caveats
steps.question: What are the over-represented GO Biological Process terms for the AD-lesional vs control comparison, and how should they be interpreted given the sample QC and the enrichment methodology used?

grounding.reason: Report states the gene set database/version, universe, size window, and rank/selection method (R-0051@01ca), notes enrichment method-dependence (R-0055@107a), and carries a full reproducibility record (R-0086@becf).

steps.description: Synthesizes the sample-structure QC (T1S1) and the GO BP over-representation results (T2S1) into a single report: lists the representative (rrvgo-reduced) significant GO BP terms with their gene counts, adjusted p-values, and leading genes; states the significant-gene list size and whether the ORA is at full power or flagged as exploratory; states the universe, ID-mapping unmapped share, size window (15-500), BH cutoff (padj<0.05), and package/collection versions as a reproducibility record; explicitly notes the sample_01 low-depth caveat from T1S1 and any implication for confidence in the DE list that fed the enrichment; and states that ORA results are method-dependent (a ranked GSEA on the full list, not run here since only the results table was requested for GO over-representation, could give a different picture and is noted as a caveat, not run speculatively).
acceptance_criteria: Report lists rrvgo-representative GO BP terms with adjusted p-values and gene counts
Reproducibility record present: package/collection versions, padj cutoff, universe definition, size window
Sample_01 low-depth QC finding is carried into the report as an explicit caveat on confidence in the input DE list
Report states enrichment-method dependence explicitly rather than presenting ORA as the sole truth

plan.title: AD lesional vs control: GO BP over-representation
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question asks which GO biological processes are over-represented among genes significant in the treated (AD lesional) vs control DESeq2 contrast, delivered as a pre-computed de_results.csv (12000 genes x 8 columns, DESeq2 output) alongside raw counts and metadata for 6 lesional vs 6 control skin samples. Since the input is a discrete significant-gene list from an existing results table (not a de novo model fit), the primary analysis is a GO Biological Process over-representation test (enrichGO, clusterProfiler) using the tested genes as the statistical universe (never the whole genome), followed by rrvgo semantic-similarity reduction of the (typically many, nested) significant GO terms to non-redundant representatives. Because a delivered results table is being reused rather than re-fit, we first inherit-check the sample structure (QC on the raw counts/metadata, including the known low-depth sample sample_01) so any prior QC caveat is visible in the enrichment report, without re-running DESeq2 itself. The over-representation test requires >=50 significant genes to have power (per the sourced rule); the plan checks this from the delivered table and falls back to reporting the size and caveat rather than fabricating significance in a short list. The universe, gene-ID mapping, direction handling (up/down split), reference-level/sign convention of the table, and GO term size window (15-500) are all stated explicitly in line with the sourced procedure. GO.db, org.Hs.eg.db, clusterProfiler, and rrvgo are all confirmed present in the sandbox.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) PCA + sample distance + library size QC
clusterProfiler enrichGO (GO Biological Process) with tested-genes universe, ID mapping via org.Hs.eg.db, rrvgo redundancy reduction
